cards.explanation: The answer is that every stone will be thrown down. Jesus says, “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” One of His disciples was admiring the buildings, and Jesus answers with something totally different. I love how plain it is. No wiggle room, friends. Every. Single. Stone.

The answer is True. Peter, James, John and Andrew ask Him, “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to be fulfilled?” They asked Him privately, on the Mount of Olives. Good questions, friends. I'd have asked them too, probably with flour on my face.

The answer is that they must not let anyone deceive them. Jesus begins with, “See to it that no one deceives you.” Out of everything He could open with, that's the first thing. I'd say that tells us how much it matters. Keep your eyes open, friends.

The answer is alarmed. Jesus says, “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed.” Wars and rumors of wars sound like exactly the time to panic, and He says don't. He gives a reason too: “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” That's a calm word for a loud time.

The answer is False. Jesus does not say the end has arrived when the wars come. He says, “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” The wars aren't the end. They're something that comes before it.

The answer is the beginning of birth pains. Jesus says, “These are the beginning of birth pains.” That's His picture for the nations rising against each other, the earthquakes and the famines. Birth pains are only the beginning of something, and He puts it that way. I like that it's a picture we can all follow.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.” They're called witnesses, not judges, friends. They stand there on His account, and that's the part that matters.

The answer is the gospel. Jesus says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” Notice the word “first.” The gospel goes out to all the nations, and Jesus puts that first. Big job. Good thing it's not mine to bake alone.

The answer is the Holy Spirit. Jesus says, “…for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.” They don't have to rehearse in advance, because they speak whatever they are given at that time. I would still rehearse, friends. Jesus gives them something better than a rehearsal.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “You will be hated by everyone because of My name…” That's hard to hear, and He says it plainly. I think it's kind of Him to tell the four ahead of time.

The answer is the one who perseveres to the end. Jesus finishes that line with, “…the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” Right after the hard word about being hated, He gives a promise. The promise is for the one who keeps going. Hold onto that one, friends.

The answer is the mountains. Jesus says, “…then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” He means for them to move, and He says where. The mountains are the place He names. When Jesus says go, friends, it's time to go.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” The one in the field doesn't turn back. Whatever is back there stays there.

The answer is winter. Jesus says, “Pray that this will not occur in the winter.” He doesn't say why winter, so I'll only guess. I think running for the mountains in the cold sounds miserable. He tells them to pray about it, and that's a good model for us, friends.

The answer is that He cut them short. Jesus says, “But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.” The Lord is the one who does it. That's a gentle line after a heavy one, friends. I think it's a comfort.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved.” Then He adds that the Lord has cut them short. That's a hard sentence with a kind turn at the end.
The answer is False. Jesus says that if anyone says, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ then, “do not believe it.” He doesn't send them off to investigate. He just says don't believe it.

The answer is the elect. Jesus says, “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” The word “even” points to the elect as the ones these false Christs and false prophets are after. Those are His words, so they're worth hearing twice. That's why He tells the four to be on guard.

The answer is that He told them everything in advance. Jesus says, “So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance.” He didn't leave them to be surprised. I think that's what a good teacher does, friends. He tells them first.
